app_summary: An online shop selling astronomy products, based on the OpenTelemetry Demo. It is built with polyglot microservices (Go, Java, .NET, Python, Node.js, Rust, ...) communicating via gRPC and HTTP behind an Envoy frontend-proxy, with Kafka for asynchronous order processing and Valkey as cart store. Supported Operations: View product catalog, Receive product recommendations and ads, Add item to cart, Checkout with selected items, Currency conversion, Process payment, Generate shipping quotes, Send order confirmation emails

args.diagnosis: Frontend-proxy (Envoy) is missing/incorrect configuration for the shipping upstream (host/port/cluster), causing a routing/cluster-name mismatch even though the shipping Service and Pod endpoints are healthy.
args.reasoning:
1) frontend-proxy pod spec (kubectl describe) shows many service host/port env vars but no SHIPPING_HOST or SHIPPING_PORT provided — the proxy container is not being given an explicit shipping address/port to populate Envoy config.
2) The shipping Service exists at clusterIP 10.96.233.92:8080 (port name tcp-service) and its Endpoints point to pod 10.244.1.33:8080, so the backend is up and reachable on port 8080.
3) Envoy started and initialized clusters (logs show "loading 13 cluster(s)"), but without the shipping mapping from the frontend-proxy configuration the proxy may not create the expected cluster/route (or may use an incorrect cluster name/port), which explains observed connection failures between frontend-proxy and shipping in the original incident.

Next actions: (a) Ensure frontend-proxy/Envoy configuration contains shipping host/port (e.g., SHIPPING_HOST=shipping and SHIPPING_PORT=8080 or the correct cluster name), (b) reload Envoy config and verify the shipping cluster appears in the admin/config_dump, and (c) from the frontend-proxy pod run curl http://shipping:8080/get-quote and curl http://10.96.233.92:8080 to confirm connectivity and collect any ECONNREFUSED errors and matching Envoy logs/traces.
